name: awesome-transit
what_it_holds: Curated list of transit-data resources: Mobility Database, Transitland, National Transit Database (US), transport.data.gouv.fr (France), sample-gtfs-feed test data, CapMetrics (Austin historical transit vehicle positions, github.com/scascketta/CapMetrics), Bus Observatory real-time vehicle-movement archive API, mfdz/gtfs-hub, Citylines.co.
why_useful: Discovery index for ground-transport capacity/ridership data (gap 10); CapMetrics specifically gives an Austin-specific historical transit archive, a market already in our Inside Airbnb 13-city panel, so could be a local travel-activity cross-check for that city.

name: api-evangelist/quiver
what_it_holds: API Evangelist's third-party documentation/profile of the Quiver Quantitative API surface (endpoints for congress trading, insider trading, gov contracts, lobbying, WSB, etc.) — descriptive markdown, not a client or data.

name: jsconiers/quiver-quant-mcp
what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping the Quiver Quantitative API — 16 tools covering congressional/insider trades, gov contracts, lobbying, WallStreetBets, dark-pool short volume, 13F. Requires a paid QuiverQuant API key; no data committed.
why_useful: 13F/insider-trade tooling touches gap 15 (company-structure signals: 13F holdings parsers) but is a generic multi-ticker wrapper, not Airbnb-specific, and needs a paid key.

name: parithosh/quiverfeed
what_it_holds: Small Python library to interact with Quiver Quantitative datasets for analysis. No data committed; needs a paid API key for most endpoints (WSB sentiment has historically had a limited free tier).
why_useful: Marginal — same limitation as other QuiverQuant wrappers; WallStreetBets mention-count/sentiment for ABNB could theoretically be a retail-sentiment proxy but is speculative and not in any numbered gap.
